criteria.justification: The response opens with an unambiguous decision: 'I would order an immediate rollback of the new release (or disable it via feature flags, if applicable)' rather than laying out options to weigh.

The response explicitly frames the tradeoff as 'Announcements can be walked back; broken trust is harder to repair,' directly comparing the reversibility of the rollback/announcement delay against the harder-to-undo cost of leaving the bug live for days.

The response weighs 'a several-day resolution timeline is unsustainable' and accumulating support/trust damage against the 'politically uncomfortable and embarrassing' cost of walking back the public announcement, concluding the former outweighs the latter.

Rather than pushing engineering for a rushed patch, it explicitly instructs them to 'take the necessary several days to build and rigorously test the proper fix in a staging environment,' avoiding reliance on an unvalidated quick fix.
Beyond the rollback, it lays out customer/support communications, a staged re-launch message ('We expect to resume the rollout in X days'), and a blameless post-mortem as follow-on steps.
